claims.text: State-of-the-art NLI systems trained on SNLI show substantial performance drops on a test set requiring simple lexical and world knowledge.
Incorporating external lexical knowledge from WordNet via KIM substantially outperforms standard neural models on the lexical inference test set.
ESIM prediction accuracy on test pairs increases as the frequency of those replacement word pairs in training contradiction examples increases.
Decomposable Attention accuracy decreases on contradicting word pairs as the cosine similarity of their pre-trained embeddings increases.

evidence.description: Accuracy on the new test set dropped by 32.8 points for Decomposable Attention, 22.3 points for ESIM, and 23.8 points for Residual-Stacked-Encoder when trained on SNLI.
KIM achieves 83.5% accuracy on the new test set compared to 65.6% for ESIM when trained on SNLI.
ESIM accuracy rises from 40.2% for replacement pairs with 0 training occurrences to 98.5% for pairs with 100+ occurrences.
Decomposable Attention accuracy declines monotonically from 46.2% for embedding similarity 0.5-0.6 down to 20.2% for similarity 0.9-1.0.

methodologies.name: Adversarial Lexical NLI Test Set Construction
methodologies.description: Automatic generation of sentence pairs by replacing single words in SNLI training premises with known vocabulary, followed by crowdsourced manual verification.
conditions: Words present in SNLI training set and GloVe vocabulary

limitations.text: Due to its heavy bias towards contradiction, the constructed test set cannot be used for training or serve as a primary evaluation set for NLI.
WordNet-informed models leave room for improvement due to limited WordNet coverage and challenges applying lexical inferences in context.
Existing neural NLI systems relying solely on pre-trained word embeddings are limited in generalization ability and fail to capture simple lexical inferences.

future_work.text: Develop NLI methods and models that capture simple lexical and world knowledge inferences more effectively.
